feature: Chip styles: the four that scored under the bar, reworked
summary: Glass is now real frosted glass: the picture behind the label shows through, softened and lightened, on the canvas and in an export. Spec badge reads as a dark Mac badge, and Highlighter marks the whole line of words instead of a tilted stripe.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walks: Scripts/playtest/glass-chip-frost-walk.json and chip-styles-walk.json. Sheets drawn by the real renderer: PHOTONZ_CHIP_SHEET=<dir> Scripts/test.sh --filter ChipStyleRendering.

try.do: Open a busy screenshot, press A, drag an arrow, type a label and press Command Return.
Right click the arrow and choose Chip Style > Glass: the label sits on frosted glass, the picture softened behind it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the arrow over a white area, then a dark one: Glass stays light frosted glass with dark words on both.
Pick Spec badge, then Highlighter, from the Chip tiles in Appearance.
Compare the reworked styles in two colours on a light window, a dark window and a photo.
Export the picture as a PNG and compare the Glass chip with the canvas.

evaluate: Does Glass read as glass to you now, or as a pale pink pill?
Does Spec badge stand off a dark screenshot well enough?
Does the Highlighter band look like a highlighted label, or like a box inside a box?
Should the set stay at ten, or drop the styles that keep scoring under the bar (see the card on this task)?
rough: The visual bar is not met. Three blind judges scored the sheet (median of three): Squircle 7, Spec badge 7, Paper 6, Solid pill 6, Hairline 6, Lit tag 6, Two-tone 5, Today 5, Glass 4, Highlighter 4, baseline 5. The first single judge on 2026-10-31 passed Solid, Hairline, Paper and Two-tone; this stricter panel does not. Whether to keep all ten is the open decision card on this task.
Lit tag: a bevel (judged dated, 4) and a glow in its own colour (judged a smudge, 4) were both tried and dropped; it is back to the approved lit fill with small corners (6).
Glass judges still call it a pale pink pill rather than Liquid Glass: on a flat sheet its see-through quality barely shows. The real app does frost what is behind it (the photo walk's picture).
Glass stands in as one opaque colour where there is no picture to frost: the style tile, the bubble while you type, and a chip being dragged.
Lifting Glass to light frosted glass changed its words to dark for every ink; markup.md section 3 and markup.js say so, and the sweep fixture was regenerated.

Contrast measured off the pixels, every palette ink over white, black, a busy photo and a saturated colour: Glass worst 8.2:1, Spec 9.4:1, Lit tag 4.7:1, Highlighter 7.1:1 (2026-11-01-chip-contrast.tsv). Export against canvas: 0 difference in every style (2026-11-01-chip-export-parity.tsv).
